summary: Retire exact owner legacy leases after verified terminal delivery

delivery.outcome: Offer explicit owner-bound retirement of expired legacy allocation projections after verified merged delivery, preserving exact original bytes without changing canonical identity acceptance.
nonGoals: No widening of ordinary lease validation, release, settlement or writer authority
No identity normalization, live/frozen lease retirement, takeover or checkout/ref deletion
No host-specific task or operational receipt stored in the hub

architecture.decision: Ship a separate opt-in adapter reusing the canonical controller directory, lock and Git receipt checks. Validate a read-only canonical-identity view of the otherwise exact legacy record; retain original bytes in a CAS-bound write-ahead journal before unlinking only the expired finished slot. Never persist a normalized lease.
interfaceChanges: Explicit legacy terminal owner retirement request/plan/apply CLI
dataChanges: Owner-private immutable journal preserves exact original legacy bytes and verified merged receipt before retirement
architecture.rollback: Revert through protected publication; original bytes remain preserved. Never restore an active slot automatically.

validation.evidence: Real Git merge/receipt fixtures, read-only plan, owner-only apply, exact archive bytes, unchanged canonical rejection and idempotency.
Negative owner/repository/phase/CAS/path/receipt cases and write-ahead interruption recovery preserve existing bytes.
Managed package, fresh exact-head/base required CI and independent Validator App publication.
